# Security model of the browser client

## Identity and keys

* **Holochain identity**: generated and held by HWC's Lair keystore inside the
  extension, bound to the browser profile, the unpacked extension location and
  the site origin. The page never sees private keys; actions are signed in the
  extension. Moving an unpacked extension can change its ID and storage.
* **Recipient key (X25519)**: generated by WebCrypto as non-extractable, stored
  as a `CryptoKey` in the site's IndexedDB, keyed by the HWC agent. Only the
  public half is ever exported.
* **Content keys**: unwrapped with `unwrapKey` straight into non-extractable
  AES-GCM keys usable only for `decrypt`; never stored, logged or sent.

## What the browser verifies itself

| Item | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Installed app | downloaded hApp SHA-256 equals the release config; each role's DNA hash equals the pinned value and the cell belongs to this agent; extra cells refused |
| Catalogue records | native `validate_track` contract; record author equals claimed artist; profiles/albums author-bound |
| Artist key | exactly one `owner-manifest` S2 key binding authored by the artist (ambiguity refused) |
| Manifest | canonical-JSON SHA-256 equals the track's `manifest_sha256` pin; artist Ed25519 signature; structure (`_assert_manifest`); owner file commitment |
| Host | replica claim, `host-receipt` key binding, endpoint record authored by the host, loopback/RFC1918 URL policy, signed receipt matching the claim |
| Chunks | length + SHA-256 per signed manifest, then AES-256-GCM with AAD = domain ‖ file_id ‖ index (reordering, substitution, truncation all fail) |
| Grant | all v1 rules (see [grants.md](grants.md)) including expiry against the browser clock |
| Audio | canonical WAV PCM16 header consistent with the signed length |

The media adapter's own checks are defence in depth only.

## Trust boundaries

* **H2HC gateway** — authenticates the browser agent (signed challenge) and
  enforces operator admission (SQLite allow-list; revocation tested). It sees
  which DHT data the listener queries and publishes the listener's signed
  actions; it cannot sign as the listener.
* **Media adapter** — sees which track, host and chunk indices a listener
  fetches (listening metadata) and ciphertext only. It can deny service; it
  cannot substitute content undetected. GET-only, exact-origin CORS, no request
  logging, refuses DNS names, public IPs, non-HTTPS and (unless `--allow-lan`)
  RFC1918 hosts.
* **Web origin** — must be HTTPS (localhost only for development). The static
  server sends `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
  connect-src 'self' <gateway> <adapter>; …; frame-ancestors 'none'`,
  `nosniff`, `no-referrer`, COOP. HWC's injected API works under this CSP
  (verified). All remote text is inserted with `textContent`.
* **Desktop loopback server** — untouched and not exposed; the web client does
  not use it.

## Remaining vulnerabilities and limits (be explicit)

1. **DHT read integrity (was HIGH; mitigated by an HWC patch, partial).**
   Unpatched HWC at the pinned commit accepts whatever the gateway returns for
   `get`/`get_details`/`get_links`, so a malicious gateway could forge
   catalogue, key-binding and endpoint records under a real artist's identity
   (and pair them with a forged grant for attacker-encrypted audio; it still
   cannot decrypt genuine content or use a real artist's key). The build now
   applies [`web/hwc/record-verification`](../../web/hwc/record-verification/README.md):
   every record is hash- and signature-verified and bound to the requested
   hash before it reaches the cache, validation or WASM, and interop check M1
   proves a tampering gateway cannot put a forged title in front of the
   listener. **Still gateway-trusted:** link authorship (the accepted gateway
   strips `CreateLink` signatures — it can hide links, or add links to
   genuine records, which are then verified), `count_links`, agent-activity
   responses and reported validation status (denial of service, not forgery).
   Needs a gateway change to return signed `CreateLink` actions. Not
   production-ready until that and an external review are done.
2. **Private grant delivery over `call_remote` (new, experimental).** See
   [call-remote.md](call-remote.md). Trust classification of what the gateway
   can and cannot do:
   * **Cannot**: sign or impersonate an agent (it never holds keys; outgoing
     provenance must equal the session agent and the signature must verify;
     the recipient re-verifies anyway); make a browser execute an unsigned,
     replayed, expired, wrongly addressed or ungranted call (HWC authorises
     every incoming call itself: SHA-512 signature, cell, persistent nonce,
     live `CapGrant`); forge a grant (grants are artist-signed and verified
     against the artist key read through the listener's own cell).
   * **Gateway-trusted (same as native transport)**: the `ZomeCallResponse`
     returned for an outgoing call is not signed by the recipient in Holochain
     either. A malicious gateway could claim a request was stored when it was
     not ("awaiting" would then never turn into a grant) or drop deliveries
     (denial of service). It cannot make "granted" appear: that state needs a
     verified, artist-signed grant on the listener's own chain.
   * The out-of-band import (recovery) still depends on the operator conveying
     the browser's public keys to the artist authentically.
   HWC's older remote-signal signing (blake2b-256) is unchanged and stays
   behind Imposter's fail-closed gate; call_remote uses its own SHA-512 path.
3. **Extension service-worker caching** — after rebuilding an unpacked HWC at
   the same version, reload it in `chrome://extensions`; an old profile can
   otherwise keep running the previous build.
4. **Plaintext exists in memory during playback** (decrypted chunk, Float32
   blocks in the AudioWorklet). Look-ahead is bounded (~6 s) and buffers are
   discarded; nothing is persisted. A legitimate listener can always record
   what they hear; browser playback is not DRM.
5. **Metadata exposure** to gateway and adapter operators (what is browsed and
   played) and to DHT peers (public catalogue reads).
6. **Clock**: streaming-grant expiry uses the browser clock (as native uses the
   OS clock); licences have no expiry by design.
7. **Not production-reviewed**: no external security review, no public
   deployment, and the IPv4-only `LD_PRELOAD` shim in `web/integration/env/`
   is for IPv6-less test sandboxes only.
